text: First cut (2026-08-09): the user deliberately deferred deterministic replay and seed storage, overriding dragons-hoard-next-steps.md which says to prove replay from DB rows before anything else. Testing is intentionally light ('worth their cost'). Stated intent: add LLM agents as the next step (user was half-considering adding them from the get-go). Also: on a wake night the hoard refills to 250 and regrowth/wake-roll are skipped — spec wording chosen over sim-hazard.py, which regrew after the refill (250->280); the Monte Carlo test in main/tests.py mirrors the engine, not the sim script.

Agent-day smoke against real DeepSeek (deepseek-v4-flash, 2026-08-10): one full game day = 150 LLM calls, ~6.6 min wall clock, ~1.0M input / 19K output tokens, est $0.20-0.35/day (system prompt gets server-side cache hits). Beat latency: parley windows ~60-80s, moot ~2.3min, night ~25s, diaries ~2.2min. Critical operational lesson: with the model's reasoning/thinking left enabled, single calls hung 15+ minutes (reasoning tokens stream forever, read timeout never fires) and 20% of calls returned empty content after burning the output budget on reasoning. Fix lives in main/llm.py (thinking disabled via extra_body, max_tokens backstop, 120s timeout) - do not remove those settings without re-testing a live day. With thinking on, a day would cost ~175x more output tokens and take 30+ min.

The audience day page shows individual Moot ballots on purpose. Ballot secrecy is an in-game rule enforced only at the prompt level (agents see just tallies); the audience plane sees everything and nothing flows back to agents, so exposing per-thief ballots leaks nothing into the game. Stavros confirmed this intent — don't 'fix' the page by hiding ballots.

Private goals (2026-08-11): user wants goal difficulty balanced across the ten thieves. Merrick's hoard checkpoint was deliberately softened from 240 to 200 at dawn of day 10 for balance - don't harden it back without playtest evidence. Three thieves (Sable, Old Nan, Joss) intentionally share the law_passed condition so they compete for the one-law-per-day slot; that rivalry is a feature, not an oversight. Goal payouts are announced publicly at dawn but the goal text/condition must never appear on any public surface (roster, context of other thieves, dawn report).

Implementor decisions (2026-08-11, Stavros): (1) Enacted Lua code is NOT shown to thieves at all - spec says code is 'readable by any agent who asks', but the user overrode this to protect thief context budgets; thieves vote on prose and must trust the code. Revisit only if a run shows they need it. (2) Parley interception and metadata-reveal capabilities are deferred until after the implementor pipeline ships; they stay OUT of the prompt capability list until built, so no law targets a power the guild cannot grant. (3) Implementor and reviewer both run on claude-fable-5 via Anthropic's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, configured by separate env vars from the thief model.

Deliberate spec deviations in the implementor build (2026-08-11, approved by Stavros): (1) announce() publishes immediately as a public event rather than queueing for the literal next dawn report - simpler, same in-world effect; the thief-facing prose was reworded to match ('words the whole village hears'). (2) The smoke test runs each of the five hooks once with synthetic args in canonical day order, NOT the spec's full synthetic day - user accepted seeing the shallow version fail in practice before building day-simulation scaffolding. (3) RuleSet rows carry code+scratchpad+proposal FK only; the spec's audit columns (diff, model id, prompt version) were rejected because LlmCall rows already record every implementor/reviewer message. (4) The inactive list is read at each beat's start; mid-beat inactivation takes effect next beat (commented at call sites).
